reasoning: This workflow automatically classifies incoming customer support messages for FairTix, a fair ticket marketplace. It monitors Gmail every minute for messages with 'Support Request' in the subject, uses Claude AI to categorize them (FAQ, Account/Verification, Payment/Billing, etc.) and assess sentiment (positive, neutral, frustrated, angry), then logs the classification to Google Sheets. The AI prompt reveals FairTix's core business model: fair queue system for ticket purchases, transparent pricing, resale caps, and phone verification. The workflow has two triggers - scheduled Gmail polling and a Google Sheets trigger as fallback. With 198 versions and extensive prompt refinement, this appears to be a critical support triage system. The 6% error rate likely comes from AI parsing failures or API limits.
name: Support Ticket Auto-Classifier
businessNarrative: This workflow automates the first-touch triage of customer support emails for FairTix, classifying them into actionable categories and sentiment levels. It enables support agents to prioritize angry customers with payment issues over neutral FAQ questions, significantly reducing response time for critical cases. The detailed classification prompt reveals FairTix operates a fair ticketing marketplace with features like random queue selection, price-capped resales, and identity verification - suggesting they're combating ticket scalping in the secondary market.

dataFlow: Support emails from Gmail → AI classification (category, sentiment, confidence) → Structured data logged to Google Sheets for agent review and routing
